mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant for two consecutive months above 5.0%, market expectations for future rate cuts increase, lowering real discount rates and boosting equity present-value pricing, which drives a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: FOMC holds or cuts rates after a prolonged period of tightening
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns in qualifying periods are not statistically higher than the 30-day risk-free rate minus the expected rate path (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points in the same month
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening in the absence of inflationary pressures
failure_condition: Over a 12-month rolling window, the correlation between the labor signal and SPX 20-day returns is below 0.3 in absolute value.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average, when accompanied by a decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL), predicts that firms will increase investment in output capacity, lowering near-term financing costs and driving a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > INDPRO_12MA AND CPIAUCSL < CPIAUCSL_12MA for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Easing supply constraints with stable or falling inflation
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero after controlling for the supply and inflation proxies (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (HOUST) unexpectedly surge by more than 2% in a month and coincidently the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0%, it indicates resilient consumer demand, which elevates earnings growth expectations and supports a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >2% month-over-month AND UNRATE < 4.0% in the same month
regime_hint: Resilient consumer demand in a low-unemployment environment
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns during qualifying events are not significantly above the mean of prior 20-day returns (bootstrap p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% for three consecutive months, without a corresponding rise in CPIAUCSL, is interpreted as a labor-market-led inflationary pressure, prompting the Fed to maintain higher policy rates, which compresses equity discount rates and produces a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5 for three consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < CPIAUCSL_12MA
regime_hint: Low unemployment with stable or declining inflation
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns during such regimes are not statistically lower than during comparable high-unemployment periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden, one-time spike in payroll employment (PAYEMS) exceeding prior month by 50,000 jobs in a month when the unemployment rate (UNRATE) remains unchanged signals a strong labor market shock that boosts investor confidence, resulting in a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >50,000 AND UNRATE is unchanged from prior month
regime_hint: Sudden payroll surge without labor market adjustment
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns during such events are not statistically higher than during baseline payroll growth (<10,000) periods (bootstrap p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 3% in two months followed by a rebound above its 12-month moving average predicts a temporary supply shock that raises risk aversion, compresses equity valuations, and produces a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >3% for two consecutive months AND INDPRO > INDPRO_12MA in the third month
regime_hint: Short-term supply disruption after a recovery
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns during such episodes are not significantly lower than during stable supply conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.5% for the first time in a tightening cycle, it signals persistent policy tightening, which raises real borrowing costs and reduces equity discounting, producing a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS_3MA > 5.5 for the first time in a 6-month tightening window
regime_hint: Initiation of a sustained policy tightening phase
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns during such events are not statistically lower than during prior non-tightening 3-month FEDFUNDS > 5.5 periods (t-test p > 0.05).
